privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.standfirst: What NphiesCore stores, who can see it, where it lives, and what leaves it. This describes the app you are holding, not a template someone filled in.
privacy.scopeBody: NphiesCore is a private work tracker for one team. It exists so that a small group running several domains can capture actions, follow them up and report on them without holding it all in their heads.
privacy.scopeNoSignup: There is no public sign-up. An administrator creates every account and hands over a one-time code in person, and the account does not work until its owner sets a password with that code. Nothing here is sold, and there is no advertising of any kind.
privacy.storedIntro: All of it lives in the workspace's own database. Every line below names a real table, not a category.
privacy.storedAccountBody: The username you sign in with, your display name, whether you are an administrator or a member, your interface language, and the date the account was made. An account created for you authenticates as ⁦username@opstrack.internal⁩ — a reserved address that can never receive mail — so the app sends you no email and keeps no mailbox for you. Your password is held by ⁦Supabase Auth⁩ as a hash and is never visible to the app.
privacy.storedWorkBody: Items, with their title, description, type, status, priority, owner, requester, due date, follow-up date, tags and links. The update thread under each item. Meetings, and every line typed during one, in the shorthand it was typed in. Recurring templates. The tracks, groups, vocabulary and wording an administrator has configured.
privacy.storedThreadBody: The update thread is append-only, and the database enforces that rather than the app: there is no rule permitting an update or a delete on it, for a member or an administrator alike. A correction is a new line.
privacy.storedNotifyBody: One row for each thing addressed to you, holding the item's title, who acted, and when you read it. If you allow push, one row for each browser or phone you allowed it on, holding that device's push address and its two encryption keys.
privacy.storedAiBody: If the capture assist is on, one row per person per day, counting how many suggestions were asked for and what they cost in tokens. It holds no line you typed, no suggestion you were shown, and no hash of either — it is a spend ledger, and it answers how much, never about what.
privacy.storedGuardsBody: Short-lived counters keyed by username or network address, so repeated failed attempts slow down. They live in rolling windows measured in seconds, and a scheduled pass clears them.
privacy.storedDeviceBody: Your theme, your language, a copy of the item list so the app opens instantly and works offline, and anything you captured while offline that has not been sent yet. All of it is ordinary browser storage under this app's own keys, readable by nothing else. Clearing the site's data, or deleting the app, removes it.
privacy.whoBody: This is a shared workspace and it behaves like one. Every signed-in member can read the tracks, the items, the update thread, the meetings and the roster. That is deliberate: the team is small, and work hidden from each other is work nobody follows up.
privacy.whoRls: The database decides this row by row, not the app. Every rule asks whether the caller holds a profile in this workspace — not merely whether they are signed in — and sign-up is switched off, so an account nobody here created can read nothing at all.
privacy.whoPrivateNotif: Your notifications. Only the recipient can read them, and there is no “who else was told”.
privacy.whoPrivatePush: Your push subscriptions. Owner-only, and not readable by an administrator either — a push address is a capability to send to that device, and nobody needs to hold somebody else's.
privacy.whoPrivateAi: Your AI usage row. Yours alone, so that “who has been leaning on the assist” is not a question one colleague can ask about another.
privacy.whoAdmin: An administrator can additionally create and remove accounts, change roles, and edit the workspace's tracks, groups, vocabulary and wording.
privacy.whereBody: One ⁦Supabase⁩ project — ⁦PostgreSQL⁩, its authentication service and its edge functions — hosted in ⁦ap-northeast-2⁩ (Seoul). Every connection is ⁦HTTPS⁩. The app itself is a static page served from ⁦GitHub Pages⁩, and the ⁦iOS⁩ app is that same page inside a native shell, so there is no second copy of the data anywhere.
privacy.aiOff: It goes off in one tap, per person, from the Settings page under AI assist. While it is off nothing leaves the app for this feature at all. While it is on, a suggestion is asked for only when a line reads like a sentence rather than the shorthand, and only once you have stopped typing.
privacy.aiSentLine: The single line you are typing, exactly as typed, with invisible control characters removed.
privacy.aiSentNames: The names and identifiers of this workspace's tracks and members. They are read on the server using your own sign-in, so the request can never carry something you cannot already see.
privacy.aiSentToday: Today's date and your interface language, so that “next Thursday” lands on the right day.
privacy.aiSentLabels: The workspace's own type and priority labels, so a suggestion can only offer a value this workspace actually has.
privacy.aiNotEntries: No items. No titles other than the line in the box. No descriptions.
privacy.aiNotThread: No update thread, no comments, no meeting lines, no minutes.
privacy.aiNotFiles: No files and no attachments — the app stores none.
privacy.aiNotIdentity: Not your address, not your password, not your notifications, not your usage.
privacy.aiNotElse: Nothing from any other screen, and no record of anything you asked for before: each request stands alone.
privacy.aiWho: The request goes to ⁦Anthropic⁩'s ⁦Claude⁩ API over ⁦HTTPS⁩, from the workspace's own server rather than from your browser. The key that pays for it belongs to the workspace owner and is held as a server secret; it is never in the app and never on your device.
privacy.aiKept: Afterwards the server records the number of requests and the token totals, and nothing else. The line and the suggestion are not stored, not cached and not logged — the error log carries failure codes and upstream status lines only.
privacy.aiNever: A suggestion only ever puts words into the box in front of you. Nothing is filed on your behalf, and your own words are never rewritten.
privacy.aiThird: What happens at the far end is governed by Anthropic's own terms.
privacy.pushBody: If you allow them, your browser or phone issues an address for that device and the app stores it. A notification carries the item's title and the name of whoever acted, encrypted for that device alone — the relay that carries it (⁦Apple⁩, ⁦Google⁩ or ⁦Mozilla⁩, depending on the device) can see that a message went by, not what it says. Turn them off from the Settings page under Notifications, or in the operating system.
privacy.pushNative: The ⁦iOS⁩ app does not use push at all. Inside the native shell the feature reports itself unsupported and never subscribes, so installing from the App Store creates no push address and no row.
privacy.notTitle: What this app does not do
privacy.notAnalytics: No analytics, no telemetry, no crash-reporting service, no advertising, no third-party trackers. The only destinations it ever talks to are the workspace's own ⁦Supabase⁩ project and, while the assist is on, ⁦Anthropic⁩'s API.
privacy.notDevice: No location, no contacts, no photos, no camera, no microphone, no health or fitness data. The only permission it ever asks the operating system for is permission to show notifications.
privacy.notSell: Nothing is sold, rented or handed to anyone for their own purposes, and nothing is tracked across other apps or websites.
privacy.keepBody: Work is kept for as long as the workspace keeps it — nothing expires on a timer, and closed items stay because the reports count them. Sign-in guard counters clear within minutes. The copy on your device is replaced on every sync and disappears when you clear the site's data.
privacy.deleteBody: Accounts here are created by an administrator, and today they are removed by one: the Settings page, under Members — choose the person, Delete, confirm.
privacy.deleteWhat: Removing an account deletes the sign-in identity and the profile, and takes with it that person's notifications, their push subscriptions on every device, and their AI usage rows. The work they filed stays — an item does not stop existing because the person who wrote it left — and their display name is copied onto that work in the same instant, so the history still names them.
privacy.deleteSelf: There is no self-service delete in the app yet, and this page says so rather than implying otherwise. An administrator cannot remove their own account from that screen either: the server refuses a self-delete, refuses to remove the last remaining administrator, and protects the workspace owner's account. To have your own account removed, ask an administrator. If you are the administrator, the workspace owner removes it directly in ⁦Supabase⁩.
privacy.askBody: To see, correct or remove what is held about you, speak to your workspace administrator. Every account here was created by one, and they are the only person able to act on this workspace's data.
privacy.changesBody: This page ships inside the app, so it changes when the app does. The version it belongs to is printed at the top.
